questions.stem: During meiosis, cohesin along the chromosome arms is cleaved at one stage and cohesin at the centromeres at another. What does each cleavage allow?
options: Both cleavages occur in anaphase I, first releasing the arms and then the centromeres within the same division
Arm cohesin cleavage allows crossing over in prophase I, while centromeric cleavage ends the S phase
Arm cleavage in anaphase I lets homologs separate; centromeric cleavage in anaphase II lets sister chromatids separate
Centromeric cleavage separates homologs in anaphase I, and arm cleavage separates chromatids in anaphase II
questions.why: Arms are held between homologs, so cutting them in anaphase I releases homologs; centromeres hold sister chromatids, so cutting them in anaphase II releases chromatids.

questions.stem: A principal writes to parents: "Due to unforeseen facility constraints, the ninth-grade wing will undergo a temporary reassignment." What does this diction chiefly accomplish?
options: It replaces a concrete disruption with abstractions, softening the news for an anxious audience
It establishes the principal's technical expertise by using facilities-management vocabulary
It concedes that the change is unpopular and invites parents to object
It creates urgency by naming a specific deadline for the move
questions.why: Every key noun is abstract (constraints, reassignment), so parents never learn what actually happens to their students; the vagueness is the softening.

questions.stem: A human primary oocyte completes meiosis I. Which count correctly describes each of the two resulting cells?
options: 23 chromosomes, each with a single chromatid, for 23 chromatids total
46 chromosomes, each with two chromatids, for 92 chromatids total
46 chromosomes, each with a single chromatid, for 46 chromatids total
23 chromosomes, each with two chromatids, for 46 chromatids total
questions.why: Meiosis I separates homologs but not sister chromatids, so each daughter has the haploid number with the chromosomes still duplicated.

questions.stem: A columnist writes: "Our town's new bike lane must be working — bike-shop sales are up 30 percent since it opened." Which criticism of the reasoning is most precise?
options: The writer offers no concession to opponents of the lane
The statistic measures retail activity, not whether more people ride or ride more safely
A single percentage cannot be calculated over so short a period
The writer appeals to authority instead of presenting evidence
questions.why: Sales of bicycles are not a measure of ridership or safety, so the evidence does not support the specific claim that the lane is working.

questions.stem: A child with trisomy 21 inherits two copies of chromosome 21 from the mother, and those two copies carry different alleles at several loci along the chromosome. Which event most likely produced the egg?
options: Nondisjunction in meiosis I of the mother, so one egg received both maternal homologs
Nondisjunction in meiosis II of the mother, so one egg received two identical sister chromatids
Nondisjunction in meiosis II of the father, so the sperm carried two copies
Crossing over between the two chromosome 21 homologs, which duplicated the chromosome
questions.why: Different alleles mean the two copies are homologs, not sister chromatids, and only a meiosis I failure sends both homologs into one cell.

questions.stem: Paragraph three lists a district's rising graduation rate. Paragraph four begins: "None of that matters if the buildings are falling down." What is the function of that opening sentence?
options: It concedes that the earlier evidence was inaccurate
It summarizes the argument the writer has made so far
It introduces an opposing view the writer will go on to defend
It reframes the earlier evidence as irrelevant to the writer's real criterion
questions.why: The sentence does not dispute the graduation data; it demotes it, declaring a different standard decisive, which pivots the argument.

questions.stem: A testcross of a tall pea plant produces 48 tall and 52 short offspring. What is the genotype of the tall parent, and on what does that conclusion rest?
options: TT, because tall offspring outnumber short ones and tall is dominant
Tt, because a roughly 1:1 ratio means the parent passed a recessive allele half the time
tt, because short offspring appeared at all in the progeny
It cannot be determined without a second testcross against a tall plant
questions.why: A testcross is against homozygous recessive, so a 1:1 split is the signature of a heterozygote; a homozygote would give all tall offspring.

questions.stem: Senator Reyes argues that a bill's cost estimates are too low. A colleague replies: "Reyes has never run a business, so his numbers can be dismissed." Which flaw is present?
options: It assumes the conclusion it is trying to prove
It treats a broad generalization as though it were a universal law
It rejects the argument by attacking the arguer's background rather than the estimates
It mistakes a necessary condition for a sufficient one
questions.why: The reply never engages the cost figures; it disqualifies the speaker, which is an ad hominem and leaves the estimates unexamined.

questions.stem: In a population at Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, 1 in 10,000 individuals shows a recessive disorder. What fraction of the population are carriers, and how do you get it?
options: About 0.01, roughly 1 in 100, because that is q taken from the square root
About 0.0001, roughly 1 in 10,000, because that is q squared
About 0.98, because carriers are everything that is not affected
About 0.0198, roughly 1 in 50, because q = 0.01 and carriers are 2pq
questions.why: q squared is the affected fraction, so q = 0.01, p = 0.99, and 2pq = 0.0198; the wrong answers stop at q or at 1 minus q squared.

questions.stem: A student writes: "The author describes the factory closing in three sentences. This shows that the workers' lives were changed by the closure." Which revision of the second sentence is strongest?
options: The compressed description makes the disruption feel routine, which is sharper than any statement of loss
The author is right that factory closures harm workers and their families
The author should have included a quotation from one of the workers
The word "shows" should be replaced with "proves" to sound more academic
questions.why: The revision explains what the formal choice accomplishes; the others restate the content, praise the claim, or swap vocabulary without analysis.

questions.stem: A human somatic cell and a human gamete are compared. Which statement about their chromosome content is correct?
options: The gamete has 23 chromosomes: 22 autosomes and one sex chromosome.
The gamete has 23 pairs, half the number of pairs in a somatic cell.
The somatic cell has 46 pairs, that is two sets of 46 chromosomes.
The gamete has 46 chromosomes but carries only one set of genes.
questions.why: Gametes are haploid with n = 23: one of each autosome plus a single sex chromosome, while somatic cells are diploid with 23 pairs.

questions.stem: In a speech on school funding, a board member describes one student who shared a textbook with three classmates, then cites district-wide per-pupil spending. What is the effect of pairing the two?
options: The anecdote replaces the need for the statistic and carries the argument alone
The statistic undercuts the anecdote by showing that funding is adequate
The anecdote makes the shortfall concrete while the figure shows it is systemic, not one family's bad luck
Both are purely emotional appeals and have no logical role in the argument
questions.why: The story supplies a face for the problem and the number generalizes it; together they answer the objection that the story was an isolated case.

questions.stem: A karyotype arranges a cell's chromosomes into pairs. What defines the two chromosomes of a single pair?
options: They carry identical alleles at every locus along their length.
They are joined at one centromere as sister chromatids of a replicated chromosome.
They are the same length and shape and carry genes controlling the same inherited characters.
They are the maternal and paternal copies of the sex chromosomes only.
questions.why: Homologs match in size and shape and carry the same genes, though the alleles may differ; identical alleles are not required.

questions.stem: A cafeteria survey of 40 students during one lunch period finds that 85 percent want a salad bar, and the principal announces that "students have spoken." Which criticism is most precise?
options: Percentages cannot be used to describe opinions
One lunch period samples a single slice of the student body, so the result speaks only for that slice
The survey should have asked about prices instead of preferences
Forty respondents is too small a group to yield any usable information
questions.why: The defect is who was sampled, not how many: one period overrepresents students who eat then, so the claim outruns the sample.

questions.stem: An unfertilized human egg carries the sex chromosome X, and a sperm may carry either X or Y. What follows at fertilization?
options: The zygote remains haploid until the sperm nucleus enters the egg.
An X egg fused with a Y sperm produces an XY zygote with 46 chromosomes.
Two haploid gametes fuse to produce a zygote with 23 chromosomes.
The zygote's sex is set by the egg, since the egg always carries an X.
questions.why: n + n = 2n: each gamete contributes one set, so the zygote is diploid with 46, and the sperm's X or Y decides the sex.

questions.stem: A proposal argues: "Because the new policy cut hallway incidents in half, it will also raise test scores." On which unstated assumption does the argument depend?
options: Test scores are the best available measure of a school's quality
The policy was implemented fairly across all grades
Hallway incidents were unusually high before the policy began
Fewer hallway incidents actually cause higher test scores rather than coinciding with them
questions.why: The conclusion only follows if the drop in incidents is causally connected to learning, which the argument never argues and the reader never grants.

questions.stem: A cell is in anaphase I of meiosis. Which statement describes what separates and what does not?
options: Sister chromatids separate while the homologous pairs stay together.
Homologs and sister chromatids both separate at the same time.
Homologs separate, while sister chromatids stay attached at the centromere.
Centromeres divide, so every chromatid becomes an independent chromosome.
questions.why: Anaphase I pulls homologs apart; centromeric cohesin is protected until anaphase II, so sisters travel as one unit.

questions.stem: A report spends nine pages on a program's cost overruns and one sentence on the 400 students who stayed in school because of it. What does the imbalance itself accomplish?
options: It argues through proportion that cost, not results, drove the report's judgment
It demonstrates that the program was in fact too expensive to continue
It shows that the writer privately endorses the program
It proves the report is balanced because both costs and benefits appear
questions.why: Space allocation is a rhetorical choice: nine pages against one sentence weights the reader's attention toward cost without ever stating a verdict.

questions.stem: After crossing over in prophase I, one chromosome can carry DNA from both homologs. Which consequence follows by metaphase II?
options: The two sister chromatids of that chromosome are no longer genetically identical.
The chromosome carries twice as many genes as it did before the crossover.
The homologs of that pair can no longer separate during anaphase I.
Crossing over changes the chromosome number of the cell that carries it.
questions.why: A crossover swaps segments between nonsister chromatids, so the sisters differ from each other; the chromosome number is unchanged.

questions.stem: An op-ed published the morning after a city council vote opens: "By now the votes are counted, so let us talk about what the vote actually decided." What does this opening assume about its audience?
options: That readers are likely to disagree with the writer's conclusion
That the vote was close enough to be contested
That readers already know the outcome, so the writer must offer interpretation rather than news
That readers have not followed the issue and need a summary
questions.why: The clause "by now the votes are counted" treats the result as known, which is why the writer moves immediately to meaning rather than reporting.

questions.stem: A species has a haploid number of 4. How many chromosome combinations can independent assortment produce in its gametes?
options: 4 combinations
8 combinations
16 combinations
64 combinations
questions.why: Combinations equal 2^n with n = 4, which is 16; homolog pairs orient independently at metaphase I.

questions.stem: A pamphlet argues: "Dr. Lin, a Nobel laureate in physics, says our reading curriculum is outdated." What is the central problem with this appeal?
options: Nobel laureates are known to hold biased opinions about education
Expertise in physics does not qualify her to judge reading instruction
The pamphlet offers no statistics about reading scores
The claim is too modest to require any support at all
questions.why: An appeal to authority is only as good as the authority's relevance to the claim, and physics gives her no standing on literacy instruction.

questions.stem: A karyotype is prepared from a patient's cells and looks normal at every chromosome. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: The patient carries no mutation anywhere in the genome
Every protein the patient produces is correctly folded
The patient's allele frequencies match the population's
Chromosome number and large-scale structure are normal, though a single-gene disorder is not ruled out
questions.why: A karyotype shows chromosomes by size, shape and number; a substitution or small deletion is invisible at that resolution.

questions.stem: An essay claims that "every standardized test ever written measures nothing but a student's ability to sit still." Which revision strengthens the argument most?
options: Add a statistic about how long the tests typically run
Replace "sit still" with a more formal term such as "sustained attention"
Narrow the claim to tests that reward pacing over content, and qualify the scope with "many"
Move the sentence from the introduction to the conclusion
questions.why: The absolute version falls to a single counterexample; a narrowed, qualified claim can be defended with the same evidence and cannot be dismissed so easily.

questions.stem: A substitution changes a codon but the amino acid it specifies stays the same. What is the most likely effect on the finished protein?
options: The protein is guaranteed to be nonfunctional because the gene sequence changed
Little or no change, because the code is redundant, though mRNA stability or translation speed can still shift
The reading frame shifts and every downstream codon is misread
The mutation cannot be inherited, since it does not alter the protein
questions.why: A silent mutation leaves the amino acid sequence intact because several codons map to the same residue; only frame shifts garble what follows.

questions.stem: A writer argues no school should start before 8:30. A reader notes one rural district that starts at 7:15 and posts the state's highest scores. What is the strongest way for the writer to respond?
options: Acknowledge the district and explain why one case, with its other advantages, does not establish the general claim
Ignore it, because a single district is not evidence of anything
Concede the argument entirely, since a counterexample has appeared
Restate the original claim more forcefully without addressing the district
questions.why: A counterexample is answered by limiting its force, not by pretending it is absent or by abandoning a claim it does not actually refute.

questions.stem: A researcher counts 46 chromosomes in a human cell that has just completed meiosis II. What is the best explanation?
options: The cell never entered meiosis and is still in G1
Crossing over doubled the chromosome number during prophase I
Nondisjunction left the cell with a diploid set, so it is not a normal gamete
Meiosis II restores the diploid number before fertilization
questions.why: A normal product of meiosis II is haploid with 23 single-chromatid chromosomes; a full set of 46 means a separation error, not a stage of meiosis.

questions.stem: "We have the plans; what we lack is the will. We have the money; what we lack is the nerve." What does the repeated structure accomplish?
options: It creates a casual, conversational tone that softens the criticism
It concedes that plans and money were never really the problem
It uses statistics to establish the urgency of the situation
It pairs each resource with a failure of resolve, so the charge lands as a pattern rather than a single complaint
questions.why: The repeated frame forces the reader to hear the same verdict twice, which turns one accusation into a diagnosis of the audience.

questions.stem: Two heterozygotes are crossed (Aa × Aa). What is the probability that a single offspring is either AA or aa?
options: One-half, because each homozygote is one-quarter and the two outcomes cannot both occur
One-quarter, because only one homozygous class can appear per cross
Three-quarters, because the dominant phenotype covers both AA and Aa
One-third, because the surviving genotypes are equally likely
questions.why: AA and aa are each 1/4 of the progeny and are mutually exclusive, so their probabilities add to 1/2.

questions.stem: A headline reads: "Officials cave to demands from activist groups." What does the verb imply?
options: That officials deliberated carefully before deciding
That officials surrendered under pressure, framing the groups as coercive
That the groups made modest and reasonable requests
That the decision was required by law rather than chosen
questions.why: "Cave" carries collapse and capitulation, so the headline judges the decision before the reader reaches a single fact about it.

questions.stem: A human egg contains two copies of chromosome 18, and at every locus examined the two copies are identical. Which event produced this egg?
options: Nondisjunction in meiosis I of the mother, which sends both homologs to one pole
Nondisjunction in meiosis I of the father, which duplicates the paternal set
Crossing over between the chromosome 18 homologs during prophase I
Nondisjunction in meiosis II of the mother, so sister chromatids failed to separate
questions.why: Identical copies are sister chromatids, and only a meiosis II failure leaves them together; a meiosis I failure would deliver two different homologs.

questions.stem: An essay on school lunches ends: "The bell will ring at 11:42 tomorrow, and nothing in this budget will have changed." What does the ending accomplish?
options: It introduces new evidence about next year's budget
It resolves the argument by conceding that reform has failed
It returns to the ordinary schedule to imply the problem persists unless the reader acts
It shifts the essay's subject from funding to the bell schedule
questions.why: The flat detail of the bell and the unchanged budget closes on consequence rather than summary, leaving the pressure with the reader.

questions.stem: An individual heterozygous at two independently assorting loci (AaBb) is testcrossed with aabb. Which phenotypic ratio is expected among the offspring?
options: 1:1:1:1, one class for each of the heterozygote's four gamete types
9:3:3:1, the standard dihybrid ratio for two heterozygotes
3:1, because the recessive parent contributes nothing to the phenotype
1:2:1, because each locus shows incomplete dominance
questions.why: The aabb parent contributes only recessive alleles, so each of the four gametes from the heterozygote shows up directly in equal proportions.
